\begin{proof}
Let $G$ be an abelian group of order $pq$, where $p$ and $q$ are distinct primes. By Cauchy's theorem, choose $a,b\in G$ with $|a|=p$ and $|b|=q$. Since $G$ is abelian, $a$ and $b$ commute. For commuting elements of coprime orders, the order of their product is the product of their orders; hence
\[
|ab|=|a||b|=pq.
\]
Thus $ab$ has the same order as $G$. The cyclic subgroup $\langle ab\rangle$ therefore has $pq$ elements and equals $G$. Hence $G$ is cyclic.
\end{proof}
